text:
Aisha N.: Hi team — I got paid today but noticed 24% federal backup withholding on my 11/30 invoice. I sent my W-9 with ITIN last month; did that not land? My net was way lower than expected.
Sophia (People Ops): Sorry about that, @Aisha. Can you paste the paystub/invoice line or invoice ID? Ill escalate to payroll.
Aisha N.: Invoice INV-2024-118, copied line below from payment confirmation PDF:
```
Payee: Aisha N.
Invoice: INV-2024-118
Gross: $5,000.00
Federal backup withholding: 24% $1,200.00
Net paid: $3,800.00
Payment method: ACH contractor
```
Payroll Bot: Ticket created: PAY-2025 assigned to @Diego (Payroll). Priority: high (possible backup withholding on contractor).
Diego (Payroll): I pulled the payfile for 2024-11-30 ACH. Our system shows payee flagged "TIN missing" at time of file creation -> auto-applied backup withholding. Looks like the W-9 scan was attached to the HR record but Recruiting Ops created the contractor profile in the contractor system and didn't mark TIN status synced.
Diego (Payroll): Quick plan: 1) stop auto-remit of the $1,200 if still in pending bank ACH window (unlikely at this point). 2) If already remitted we will process a payroll/ACH credit for the withheld amount and then initiate state/fed reclaim where applicable. 3) Confirm docs and update contractor profile to prevent recurrence. Also confirm whether backup withholding needs to be reported on 1099 vs Form 945 handling.
Recruiting Ops: We did upload W-9 PDF on 2024-10-30 but the connector to contractor-platform failed on that date for a subset of hires; raising infra ticket to fix mapping and do backfill.
Tax Team: Note: backup withholding is federal withholding and if remitted to IRS it's reported on Form 945 reconciliation. For the contractor the withheld amount will reduce their 1099-NEC reportable net receipts, but we still need to reconcile deposits. Easiest fix for employee experience: payroll ACH credit ASAP and then we (Tax) will pursue reclaim from IRS or leave as remitted and provide docs for contractor to claim credit.
Diego (Payroll): ETA: Ill check bank ACH status within 2 hours. If ACH settled, I'll schedule an immediate off-cycle ACH credit for $1,200 and mark PAY-2025 as remediation planned. If ACH is pending we can stop remittance and issue full $5,000.
Manager - Jeff: Thanks for triaging. Aisha, do you want the payroll credit now or prefer to wait for Tax reclaim (if faster net outcome)?
Aisha N.: Id prefer the payroll credit so Im not out of pocket while the reclaim happens.
Diego (Payroll): Copy that. I found the original ACH settled at 09:42 — remittance completed. Scheduling off-cycle credit for tomorrow morning. Will include explanation memo and copy of W-9 from HR.
Tax Team: Once credit posts, we will open reclaim with IRS for the deposit. If reclaim fails or takes long, we will provide documentation for the contractor to claim credit on return. Also well adjust internal SD/IT mapping so that contractor-platform TIN flag mirrors HR upload.
Sophia (People Ops): Action items summarized:
b7 @Diego schedule off-cycle ACH credit for $1,200 (PAY-2025)
b7 @Recruiting Ops backfill W-9 sync and confirm mapping fix
b7 @Tax Team start reclaim workflow and advise on Form 945 implications
b7 @Diego confirm note in contractor record and send POC email to Aisha
Aisha N.: Thanks everyone. Please cc me on PAY-2025 updates and any docs I need to sign.
Diego (Payroll): Will do. Ill update this thread after the credit posts and close PAY-2025. :white_check_mark:
